haiku-low.q1: When enqueue_notification inserts the row inside the caller's transaction. It exists only if that transaction commits, since enqueue is all or nothing.
haiku-low.q2: It redelivers the message after 30 seconds, possibly to another consumer.
haiku-low.q3: Up to 5 attempts, retried after 1, 2, 4 and 8 minutes. After the fifth failure the row is marked failed, a status event is written, and on-call is paged.
haiku-low.q4: shipping_update first, then order_confirmed, then password_reset last. Before the last move: steps 1 to 6 complete, sweep alerts tested, 3-day dwells, and the p99 under 60 s latency gate passed.
haiku-low.q5: The notification id, set when the row is created and reused on every retry. MailRelay drops a repeat whose key it accepted in the last 24 hours.
haiku-low.q6: A publisher copies the row's fields into notification.requested and publishes it every 5 s. The monolith marks the row handed_off after broker confirm and commit, then waits for a status event.
haiku-low.q7: enqueue_notification decides, once, when the row is created. It sets route to service only if the flag equals service, otherwise monolith.
haiku-low.q8: The service inbox's primary key on notification id. A duplicate insert conflicts and is ignored and acked. MailRelay also drops a repeated idempotency key.
haiku-low.q9: It acks only after committing the inbox row, and before sending. A crash before commit means redelivery; a crash after commit means the stored row is sent later.
haiku-low.q10: In the service database's inbox table (attempts, next_attempt_at, claimed_until). The sender, polling every 5 seconds, acts on it.
haiku-low.q11: Rows already routed to the service keep flowing and report status, and nothing is re-sent. Pending service-routed rows are still published and sent by the service.
haiku-low.q12: id, type, user_id, email, payload, created_at, and version v. Email content is produced by the service's shared templates, rendering from type and payload only.

sonnet.q1: The row is durable when enqueue_notification inserts it into the monolith notifications table inside the caller's transaction (id uuid4, user, email, payload). Whether it exists is decided by that transaction committing (all or nothing). Flags only decide route.
sonnet.q2: The broker is at-least-once: an unacked message is redelivered after 30 s, possibly to another consumer.
sonnet.q3: 5 attempts total. Backoff after failures 1-4 is 1, 2, 4, 8 minutes (attempts 1 to 4 set state retry with that delay). The fifth failure sets state failed, writes a status event to outbox, and pages on-call.
sonnet.q4: Order: shipping_update (step 7, dwell at least 3 days), then order_confirmed (step 8, no unresolved sweep pages or duplicate reports, dwell at least 3 days), then password_reset (step 10). Before password_reset moves, the step 9 latency gate must pass: p99 of accepted_at minus created_at for accepted order_confirmed sends under 60 s, with retried sends counted. Step 6 shadow soak (3 days, zero mismatches) must also precede the first cutover.
sonnet.q5: idempotency_key = the notification id. It is set when the row is created (uuid4 from enqueue_notification) and reused on every retry. MailRelay drops a send whose key it accepted in the last 24 hours.
sonnet.q6: Rows with route = 'service' and status pending are picked by the monolith publisher (every 5 s), which publishes notification.requested to the broker with a confirm timeout. After the broker confirms, it sets status = handed_off and handed_off_at in the same transaction and commits. The monolith treats its part done at handed_off (then waits for a terminal notification.status event, sent or failed).
sonnet.q7: enqueue_notification decides, at enqueue time when the row is created. It sets route once to monolith or service, based on the flag notifications.route.<type> (anything else, including a flag read error, gives monolith). The route is fixed per row.
sonnet.q8: The consumer inserts into inbox with INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING (id is the primary key), so the duplicate is acked and the existing row is untouched. Also, the MailRelay idempotency_key = id would drop a repeat send.
sonnet.q9: It acks only after its own commit (insert into inbox). Never ack before commit. If it crashes in between, the message is unacked, redelivered after 30 s, and the insert conflicts or inserts harmlessly, so nothing is lost or duplicated.
sonnet.q10: In the service database inbox table (state, attempts, next_attempt_at, claimed_until, send_started_at, last_error). The service's Sender, polling every 5 s, acts on it.
sonnet.q11: Nothing changes for them. The flag affects only new enqueues (I5). Rows already routed to the service keep flowing and report status, nothing is re-sent. Rows still pending with route service keep being published by the publisher, and the service sends them. Only new enqueues go to the old worker, picked up within 5 s.
sonnet.q12: A notification.requested message with fields v, id, type, user_id, email, payload, created_at, copied by the publisher from the row. Email content is produced in the service: it renders the email (subject and body) from the shared templates package using (type, payload), without reading the monolith database.
